analysis: Examined the documentation-only change to docs/architecture/inference.md (new NAX / Nemotron Super paragraph at head lines 456-468; the supplied excerpt starts at head line 1623 and shows only unchanged surrounding text) and the libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule pointer bump (19634dd8 -> 0351444e). The doc change describes NAX kernels for NVFP4 experts, a differing expert summation order, a GPU window-submit cadence and a fusion env toggle (DARKBLOOM_NEMOTRON_SUPER_MTP_WINDOW_SUBMIT, DARKBLOOM_NEMOTRON_SUPER_MTP_FUSION). These are performance and numerics knobs on the provider's local inference engine and do not touch the coordinator wire contract, attestation, key custody, authorization, or prefix-cache storage (T-041 scope: KVCacheSSD, HMAC lookup tags, TTL, salt scoping), so no security regression follows from the doc text. The submodule bump is the material uncertainty: the new commit's contents are not supplied, so I cannot verify that it leaves MLX/mlx-swift-lm behavior unchanged for TB-007 properties (cancellation, T-010; GPU residual memory, T-028; KV/prefix-cache handling, T-041; weight handling, A-004) or introduces no new env-controlled code paths, file writes, temp-file plaintext (T-050), or network behavior. The doc claims neither change alters a token, but that is unverified here. Missing source is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety. Integration should check the submodule diff (Nemotron Super NAX kernels, MTP fused decode, window-submit changes) for those items and confirm the pinned commit is the intended reviewed revision.
